tier_reason: The README's 'SET: Throughput vs p50 Latency' scatter plot (docs/ubbl_compare.png) shows UnisonDB at about 100k-133k req/s and 0.21-0.40 ms p50, against LMDB at about 35k-42k req/s and 0.69-0.86 ms. The harness is public (internal/benchtests/cmd/redis-server/main.go, store/lmdb.go, run.sh) and the CPU is stated (Apple M2 Pro), but no Go version or build flags are given, so this is first-party C, not A.

corrections.workload: redis-benchmark against the repo's Redis-compatible Go server (internal/benchtests/cmd/redis-server, run.sh): each of 50 runs issues -t set,get with -n 200000 -r 200000 -d 1000 -c 10 -P 10 --threads 4, i.e. 200k SET then 200k GET requests with 1KB values. Only the SET throughput-vs-p50 chart is published. UnisonDB uses LMDB as its B-tree backend, WAL sync interval 1s and a 16MB memtable arena; the LMDB baseline is PowerDNS/lmdb-go opened with NoSync (periodic env.Sync), with one write transaction per SET.
corrections.caveats: First-party benchmark in its own repo; no Go version or build flags stated. Results exist only as a scatter-plot image, so the numbers are approximate, and GET results are described but not charted. UnisonDB itself uses LMDB as its storage backend. The gain comes from its WAL plus memtable buffering (WAL fsync every 1s, batched flush to LMDB) versus raw LMDB doing one NoSync write transaction per SET behind the same Redis-protocol server. It is a write-path/architecture win, not a faster core B-tree than LMDB. Low confidence.

notes: Numbers and hardware match the README chart; the record's ~3x throughput / ~3x lower p50 reading is fair (derived from page data). Metadata checks out: Apache-2.0, 426 stars, last commit 2026-09-12, not a fork, not archived. I only sharpened the workload and caveats with the harness config I saw in the source.
